summary: Verified plan v1 of build opp-amount-lock (scale: ask, build_mode: design-only) — one milestone, one step, three lenses, one round, refutation-only. `build_plan.py validate` exited 0 with 0 warnings before and after the write. No CRITICAL refutation as standards/build-orchestration.md § 3.1 defines it at this tier: metadata-builder resolves and is the § 4 design-only owner for type `validation`; both cited skills and the one template resolve; both declared checkers are on disk, accept --manifest-dir, reproduce the plan's own test descriptions verbatim against a fixture of the four declared outputs, and fail on a mismatched $Permission name; neither decision cites a tree and both carry a source_reference that resolves. Outcome: verified, with 10 warnings, two of them notable — an access-granting step carrying human_gate: false (which § 3.1 itself forces at ask scale) and a milestone manual test only a deployed org could settle. No amend-step was applied: the CLI refuses it while the build status is planned or verified, and it cannot reach a milestone's acceptance tests at all.
confidence_rationale: The rubric's HIGH row is met mechanically — all three lenses ran on the one step, every verdict carries an evidence line naming a file read or a command run with its output, and no verdict rests on a missing file. Downgraded to MEDIUM because the outcome turns on one adjudication no file settles: plan-verifier's own testability table refutes an access-granting step with human_gate: false and REFUSAL_SECURITY_GUARD says such a plan is rejected rather than warned, while § 3.1 forces human_gate: false at ask scale, bounds CRITICAL to the executability and grounding lenses, and has ensure-gates write no step: record. A human reading the other side of that contradiction would get plan-rejected from the same evidence.

Plan verification report — opp-amount-lock v1
deliverables.content: See the markdown twin at the same stem: verdict matrix, ten warnings with evidence and remedies, five cross-step results, and the G2 gate line.

findings.title: Access-granting step carries human_gate: false
findings.detail: Testability lens. M1-S01 emits a CustomPermission and a PermissionSet with human_gate: false. The testability table's 'Human gate present' row fires on a literal reading, and REFUSAL_SECURITY_GUARD would reject the plan. Recorded as a warning instead because § 3.1 forces human_gate: false at scale: ask and has ensure-gates add no step: record there; because § 3.1's CRITICAL list at ask is exhaustive and names only executability/grounding refutations; and because REFUSAL_CODES.md scopes REFUSAL_SECURITY_GUARD to a Modify-All-Data-class permission, not to the bypass custom permission admin/validation-rules ranks 'Preferred'. Mitigation verified rather than assumed: RUN.md names both artefacts in M1-S01's outputs and in the manual acceptance line, so the grant is in front of the human at the single go gate.

evidence.detail: Outputs list carries customPermissions/Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock.customPermission-meta.xml and permissionsets/Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass.permissionset-meta.xml; standards/build-orchestration.md § 3.1 'ensure-gates reads scale: at ask it adds milestone:M1 and no step: record, because the single step is written human_gate: false'

findings.title: M1 manual acceptance test is observable only in a deployed org
findings.detail: Testability lens. The M1 manual test asks a human to tick that a user's save was blocked and a Sales Ops user's save succeeded. This is a design-only build; § 3.1 says nothing deploys and that mock_deploy.py --dry-run's summary.md is the evidence the gate rests on. Every milestone manual test in examples/builds/case-onboarding is artefact-readable by contrast. Remedy: reword to an artefact-readable assertion over artefacts/M1-S01 and carry the in-org behaviour forward as a post-deploy UAT line. Not applicable at this stage — amend-step reaches step fields only and is refused at status planned/verified.

evidence.detail: M1 manual: 'when record-type-decision.md is read, then it states...'; M2 manual: 'the support manager and the admin lead jointly confirm that no named user is hard-coded in any queue or group' — both readable from artefacts, neither needing an org

evidence.detail: --manifest-dir <empty dir> printed 'Summary: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 info.' and exited 0; check_validation_rules.py on the same dir printed HIGH 'no validation rule metadata files found' and exited 1

findings.title: admin/validation-rules contradicts itself on ISBLANK over a picklist
findings.detail: Grounding lens. SKILL.md:119 gives NOT(ISBLANK(StageName)) as the GOOD example — the form the step copied — while references/llm-anti-patterns.md:169 gives NOT(ISBLANK(TEXT(Status))) for the same job. Not a refutation: the step's form is grounded in the more canonical location. If the platform rejects ISBLANK on a raw picklist the fix is TEXT(StageName). The guard is behaviourally redundant (ISPICKVAL already returns false on a blank picklist) and is present to satisfy check_validation_rules.py:418.

findings.detail: Grounding lens. The plan names the custom permission Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock; admin/custom-permissions points at Bypass_Validation_<Domain> for anything larger than a single-team org. Defensible as the single-gate shape, but the next Opportunity rule needs a second permission and a second permission set.

Surface at the go gate: the historical violations stay permanently non-conforming by design.
